question.text: Scenario: Karan Singh is advising a manufacturing company that exports automotive components. The following economic changes have occurred simultaneously: (1) RBI has cut the repo rate by 75 basis points over the last 6 months from 6.50% to 5.75%. (2) The Indian Rupee has depreciated 8% against the US Dollar from Rs.82 to Rs.88.50. (3) Global crude oil prices have fallen 25% from $90 to $67.50 per barrel. (4) India's GDP growth has improved from 5.5% to 7.0%. (5) The US Federal Reserve has started cutting rates, weakening the US Dollar globally. (6) WPI inflation has fallen from 6.5% to 3.2%. The company earns 60% of its revenue from exports (invoiced in USD) and imports 30% of its raw materials (also priced in USD). The remaining revenue is domestic, and 70% of raw materials are sourced domestically. Karan needs to assess the net impact on the company. Question 4 of 5: The combined effect of all six economic changes on this company is best described as:

answer.text: Mixed but likely positive based on the stated export and import weights
No impact as positive and negative factors cancel out exactly
Positive for revenue but negative for profitability

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 97, a rate cut is expansionary and lowers borrowing costs. Per pages 220-221 and 223-224, INR depreciation supports exporters but raises USD-priced import costs. Per page 88, falling commodity prices improve profitability. Improving GDP growth supports domestic demand, and falling WPI moderates input cost inflation. With 60% of revenue from exports and only 30% of raw materials imported in USD, the export gain on the larger revenue base is likely to outweigh the import cost increase on the smaller material base. The Trap: While 30% of imported raw materials become costlier due to INR depreciation, this is partly offset by the 60% export revenue boost in INR terms, plus lower crude and energy costs and improved domestic demand. A precise 'significantly positive' magnitude is not directly calculable from the given data. Note: The component drivers (rate cut, FX, commodities, GDP, WPI) are grounded in pages 88, 97, 220-224 and 234. Any specific global rate or EM-asset flow claim should be separately sourced before being relied upon.
